## A useful definition does three things {#l1-recap }

1. Names the variable: $X$, $T$, $H$, …
2. States exactly what it represents, including units where needed.
3. Identifies its possible values well enough to classify it.


::: {.takeaway}
“Discrete” does not mean “integer”, and “continuous” does not mean “we know every possible value”.
:::

::: notes
Exit prompt: Give a discrete variable with non-integer values, then a continuous variable that is recorded to limited precision.
:::
